headline: Public Law 113-105 directs Congress to award one gold medal to American Fighter Aces as a group and gives it to the Smithsonian.
what_it_does: The law tells the House Speaker and the Senate President pro tempore to arrange presentation of a single congressional gold medal honoring the American Fighter Aces collectively. It requires the medal be given to the Smithsonian Institution for display and research. It expresses the sense of Congress that the medal should also be displayed elsewhere, especially at places tied to the Aces. It lets the Treasury Secretary strike and sell bronze duplicates priced to cover costs.
when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on May 23, 2014. The summary does not set any other deadlines.
